us: Rubio to allies: no new strikes 'for now' · Trump: 'very big victory', 'not in a hurry' · Bessent courts Bahrain
effects: Brent $89.06 after −3% dip · Kpler: 5 transits vs 15 avg · War support 31% · Gas $4.10/gal
iran: Corridor: inbound via Iranian waters · Military ships barred · 'Militarily, the Strait of Hormuz is closed' · Araghchi takes the case to the UN
tldr: Iran and Oman moved the reopening question from rhetoric to blueprint: a temporary Hormuz corridor with inbound shipping routed entirely through Iranian waters, military vessels barred, and a permanent arrangement negotiated within 30–60 days — even as Tehran kept the strait closed and a senior Iranian source cautioned no agreement was finalised. Rubio told allied foreign ministers Washington plans no new strikes 'for now,' pivoting to economic and maritime pressure as war support sank to 31% and Trump claimed a 'very big victory' with 'no time schedule.' Brent chopped to near $86 before recovering to ~$89 as Kpler counted just five transits against a 15-vessel average.

events.title: Iran–Oman temporary corridor takes shape; Tehran: 'militarily, the Strait of Hormuz is closed'
events.summary: After Tuesday's joint statement, Omani FM Badr Albusaidi said he was 'hopeful we will soon announce a temporary corridor for the Strait of Hormuz and practical arrangements to restore safe navigation.' Wednesday brought Iran's detail: deputy FM Kazem Gharibabadi said inbound ships would transit entirely through Iranian waters, outbound through both countries', military vessels would be barred, and a permanent plan negotiated within 30–60 days. IRGC spokesman Mohebbi claimed water and revenue shares were settled and blamed US obstruction; a senior Iranian source told Reuters no agreement was finalised. Washington opposes parts of the deal — Trump has threatened to bomb Oman if it 'gets in the way' — Iran's transit-fee demand remains a sticking point, and Iranian readouts close the UN-authorized southern route along Oman's coast, which the Omani statement never mentioned. A joint demining initiative is included; experts doubt Iran can sweep the waterway.

events.title: Rubio tells allies: no new strikes on Iran 'for now'
events.summary: Axios reported Tuesday — carried on Wednesday wires — that Rubio told allied foreign ministers Washington does not currently intend fresh military strikes, focusing instead on economic and maritime enforcement. Reuters/Ipsos polling the same day put war support at 31%, its lowest since the conflict's early days, with Trump's approval at a record-low 33%. The message corroborates the strike pause but covers no new sanctions steps.

events.title: NBC News: Iranian strikes crippled US intelligence sites across the region
events.summary: Four people familiar with the matter told NBC News that drone and missile strikes hit at least 20 US government sites across eight countries — including a drone barrage on the CIA station in Riyadh and a secondary facility in eastern Iraq — with more than 2,000 Iranian projectiles fired in the war, repairs in the billions, and Congress scrambling for funds; the report credits Russia and China with satellite-imagery support. A Pentagon spokesperson declined comment; CSIS's Seth Jones: 'we got hammered.' Single originating outlet, anonymous sourcing — unconfirmed by any official.

events.title: Trump: 'very big victory'; Khamenei 'very seriously wounded' but not dead
events.summary: In Wednesday interviews with Al Jazeera and Glenn Beck, Trump claimed US financial strength is moving the country 'toward a very big victory,' said he doesn't believe Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is dead ('if he is, they're doing a very good job of maintaining the appearance'), and on talks: 'I have no time schedule; I'm not in a hurry.' Per the US Navy, all mines in the strait's international waters are removed or detonated, and any vessel laying new ones would be 'immediately and systematically destroyed'; the US is watching 'every square inch' of the waterway. He doubted Iranians can force regime change: 'it's very hard to protest when you have people that are willing to shoot you.'

events.title: Araghchi takes the sanctions case to the UN as 'economic terrorism'
events.summary: A letter to Guterres, the Security Council president and member states — released Wednesday by the Foreign Ministry, though the Reuters wire datelines it Thursday — requests a UN assessment of the humanitarian and human rights impact of US measures on food, medicine, healthcare and energy, and condemns secondary sanctions. At the Security Council, deputy representative Gholamhossein Darzi urged governments to 'reject and condemn' the campaign. 'Either we defend the principles of sovereign equality… or we surrender to the unilateralism and bullying of a rogue state.'

events.title: China emerges as the campaign's test ahead of a Xi–Trump summit
events.summary: CSIS's Edgard Kagan told AP Monday's rollout was 'very careful… to avoid specifics (against China), which could have led to a disruption in the summit' — Xi is expected in Washington next month. CNN notes China buys as much as 90% of Iran's oil, yet no Chinese banks were designated. Beijing held its line: Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said ties with Iran 'should not be disrupted or undermined' and China would take 'all necessary measures' to safeguard its interests.

events.title: Oil chops lower, then recovers; strait traffic stays marginal
events.summary: Brent fell ~3% to near $86 and WTI ~2.8% to $80 early Wednesday before a choppy recovery to $89.06 (+0.54%) and $83.04; contracts are down 9% and 8% on the week despite the 'economic D-Day' threats. Deutsche Bank analysts: traders in 'wait-and-see mode' absent penalty details or a timeline. Kpler counted five commodity vessels transiting Tuesday vs a 10-day average of 15; US crude inventories rose just 95,000 barrels vs 597,000 expected.

events.title: Bessent takes 'Operation Economic Outcast' to Bahrain
events.summary: Per Treasury's readout, Bessent spoke with Bahrain's finance minister Shaikh Salman bin Khalifa Al Khalifa about the campaign, called for sustained pressure on Iran's remaining economic lifelines, said Tehran must not be allowed to use the Strait of Hormuz 'as leverage against the global economy,' and agreed to coordinate with GCC partners on illicit finance — the campaign's most visible follow-through since Monday's launch, with no new designations announced.

events.title: Netanyahu: US measures 'tighten the siege' on Tehran
events.summary: Speaking at the Binyamin Regional Council (late Tuesday Israel time, covered Wednesday), Netanyahu praised the economic measures for targeting countries doing business with Iran — acknowledging the Trump administration 'did not take significant steps against Iran itself but against its allies' — and said 'the challenge of Iran has not yet ended.' Mint later carried his line that no agreement can be reached 'with those savages' (stamped Aug 27 IST; UTC-straddling, not filed as Aug 26).

events.title: State TV video threatens Barron Trump; Secret Service 'aware'
events.summary: A three-minute segment aired on Iranian state television claimed the president's 20-year-old son was being monitored and that a $10 million bounty had been offered for his killing; the Secret Service confirmed it is aware (Reuters). No US response announced.

dossier: Night count: 27th consecutive without confirmed strikes inside Iran. Corroborating: Rubio's no-new-strikes message (Axios via Reuters/USA Today); CENTCOM's only visible Aug 26 post was a National Dog Day item (CNN); no confirmed-strike reporting anywhere in the window; stage-2 notes flag an NBC piece (Aug 30, no URL captured) later calling Sunday's Houthi-claimed strike the 'first military action in a month' — soft corroboration only. Blockade ledger carried unchanged at 70 redirected / 3 disabled / 2 boarded — no new CENTCOM accounting found; the 71-vs-70 verification thread stays open. Carrier sustainment: USS Theodore Roosevelt (5,000 crew) deploys ~7 months — CO planning on 8 — to relieve George Washington; Lincoln stopped in Thailand after 250+ consecutive days at sea; Bush also in region; CNO Caudle: 'the enemy gets a vote' (USNI via CNN). Fars (single source, state-affiliated): an Iranian warship deterred Indian tanker HAANA from the southern 'Oman corridor'; no vessels used the route in the prior 24 hours; separately, two supertankers with 4M barrels of Saudi crude loaded for China via STS off Oman (Wednesday shipping data). Transit-fee dispute: Tehran demands passage fees — Washington rejected; Oman opposes formal fees but reportedly open to service charges. Iranian readout of the corridor closes the UN-authorized southern route along Oman's coast; the Omani statement never mentioned closing it. Timing caveats: Gharibabadi's state-TV routing detail was 'late Tuesday' (UTC-straddling); Araghchi letter dated Wednesday by CNN but 'published on Thursday' in the Reuters wire — treated as Wednesday, flagged; AP/Yahoo live page updated after Aug 26 — only Aug-26-or-earlier items used. Qatar LNG exports −96%, ~$24B in lost gas sales (Reuters via CNBC TV18); IMF's Georgieva: weathered the shock 'better than feared' but 'the energy shock is not over'; AAA $4.10/gal, August possibly a record; Brent earlier in the session −3% near $86. Iran domestic: Arvand (Mahshahr) petrochemicals suspended since Aug 22 and Ghadir shut amid heat wave and power shortages (IRNA in July: ~230M m³/day gas capacity lost since the war began); AEOI chief Eslami: damaged nuclear sites not secured for IAEA inspections, Iran in a 'wartime situation'; munitions-disposal blasts near Pakdasht; armed-forces spokesperson Shekarchi said staff of BBC/Iran International/Radio Farda could be listed as 'potential targets'; Pezeshkian: 'America will not achieve anything with economic pressure at this stage, just as it was unable to achieve anything in the war' (ISNA, Aug 27 IST stamp — hedge); Iran asked Qatar for answers on three missing Su-24 pilots; Ghalibaf mocked Bessent's D-Day rhetoric on X. Regional: Qatar PM al-Thani visits Tehran Thursday; Pezeshkian–Putin meet at the SCO Bishkek summit Sept 1 after a $25B nuclear-plants MOU (Mehr via Amb. Jalali); Japan (93% of 2025 crude via Hormuz) plans bypass-pipeline measures by year-end; US–Saudi civil-nuclear pact sent to Congress, conditioned on Saudi normalization with Israel; Dubai airport H1 passengers −31%; State Dept sending diplomats back to missions in Lebanon, Israel, Saudi Arabia and Baghdad. Ash Shishah tanker (UKMTO 120-26): TradeWinds identifies a Greek tanker adrift after the engine-room projectile hit — paywalled, single outlet, medium confidence; no attribution, claim, denial, or tow/salvage update found on Aug 26. Iranian editor Mokhtar Haddad (Al-Wefaq, via Al Jazeera): the US may be managing the standoff until the midterms — 'they are the same sanctions.'
